A.taste_why: Shows a compact "182G free" (size only when the bar is vertical). It uses caption font and a 6px margin, and hides itself until the first df result arrives. Sizes are rounded up like `df -h`, which is familiar. Clicking opens btop through `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui`. That fits Omarchy but is unrequested behaviour hidden behind a disk label. Low space is shown with `active: root.low`, i.e. the button's active styling, which may be the theme accent rather than a true red.
A.implementation_why: Clean, idiomatic BarWidget with a Process, a StdioCollector, a Timer with triggeredOnStart, and a running guard in refresh(). Weaknesses: the parsed fields are not checked with NaN/isFinite. A bad `interval` setting gives `Math.max(5, NaN)` = NaN, which breaks the Timer. Manifest schema types are plain `number` with no bounds.
A.execution_why: Shows free space on / as "NNNG free", refreshes every 60s and flags under 10% free. The red is delegated to WidgetButton `active`, which may not actually be red. The click-to-btop is an extra nobody asked for.

B.taste_why: Same "182G free" text, with a clear tooltip showing percent to one decimal. Clicking only refreshes, which is restrained. It keeps the default WidgetButton font and padding. There is no `visible` guard, so an empty button may sit in the bar before the first df run. Sizes are floored, which slightly understates free space compared with df.
B.implementation_why: Parsing is split into a readable parse() with an isNaN check. The interval has a `|| 60` fallback against bad settings. displayText and the tooltip are guarded while there is no data yet. A header comment explains the urgent-colour intent. There is a small redundant check (`availBytes >= 0` and `sizeBytes > 0` both used for low).
B.execution_why: Meets every part of the request: free space on /, a "G free" label, 60s refresh and a 10% threshold. There are no unwanted extras. As in all four builds, the red relies on WidgetButton `active` styling.

C.taste_why: Compact caption-sized label that stays hidden until it has data. It formats sensibly: whole G above 10G, one decimal under 10G, M under 1G, T above 1T. The tooltip gives % free. Click just refreshes, so there are no surprises. The settings have sensible bounds (10–3600s, 1–50%).
C.implementation_why: The most defensive of the four. It has a single hasData flag and isFinite/size>0 checks. It passes `--` before the path so a path cannot be read as a df option, and it uses `-P` for stable POSIX columns. It falls back on NaN for both settings and has a clear comment on the df output format. One risk: schema `type: "path"` may not be a supported schema type.
C.execution_why: Does exactly what was asked: a "182G free" style label for /, a 60s refresh and a 10% low threshold, with nothing extra. The red is again via `active`.

D.taste_why: formatSize always floors to whole GiB, so a nearly full disk shows "0G free". That is exactly the moment the widget matters. Left click launches btop and only middle click refreshes, which is surprising and unrequested.
D.implementation_why: Parsing is sound, with isFinite and size>0 checks, and the manifest schema has bounds. The interval setting has no NaN fallback. The formatter ignores the sub-1G and sub-10G cases. Using totals initialised to 0 as a 'no data' flag works but reads less clearly.
D.execution_why: Covers the label, the minute refresh and the 10% threshold. However, the display degrades badly when space is low, the case the request cares most about. It also adds unrequested click behaviour.

verdict.ranking_why: C is the most robust and restrained, with good formatting at every size and safe df invocation. B is clean and does exactly what was asked, but lacks a hide-until-loaded guard. A is solid but adds a btop launch and lacks NaN guards. D floors near-empty disks to "0G" and changes the click behaviour unasked.
